Snorting DMT
An alternative way of ingesting DMT is by snorting it. It is definitely painful, but also extremely effective, and does not require use of an MAOI.
The experience is intense. However, unlike smoking, I have a few minutes to sink into the experience, and the whole experience lasts longer, with a more gentle return to baseline.
The setting was alone in my room on a beautiful clear night, with candles, incense, Shpongle playing.
I snorted 2 lines, of around 200mg, which was definitely a high dose. I noted perceptual changes in under a minute and an intense nasal burn that seemed to come in waves.
It cant have been more than 5 minutes and the trip had already built to a very intense level, and I was getting anxious how far it would continue to build. I had a feeling of intense, almost electric pressure in my head and there was an intense buzzing sound/sensation, similar to strong smoked experiences. As a safety net I blew my nose to expel any remaining DMT to stop the trip escalating further.
I blew my nose to expel any remaining DMT to stop the trip escalating further.
A dose this high was definitely not necessary.
Shpongle was playing in the background, but formed a backdrop to my own vocalising. This was the most incredible part of the experience. I experimented with a range of sounds, imagine imitating a didgeridoo with your mouth and lips, and also blowing, hissing and whatever else I decided on at the time. It had a profound effect on the DMT experience, and allowed me to navigate it and guide it in some way. When I vocalised, entire scenes would unfold, feeding off the sound waves, and a change in the sound would lead to a change in the visual scenery.
I always feel amazing after vocalising. Refreshed and at peace
. It not only deepens and guides the trance, it can also prolong it.
I took a 3mg melatonin capsule before the experience, which resulted in a powerful dreamy afterglow that was very pleasant.
I wouldnt recommend snorting DMT often however. There is no doubt that is harsh on the nasal membranes.
